(KGS)' 1,350.00 are both plain decimals, and reading Amount as a weight or N.W. as the line value both produce a fully plausible declaration. title: Packing list with an L x W x H dimension column whose numbers must not be read as weights
note: China · LED lighting export, carton dimensions printed per row
what_is_different: A single cell holds three numbers joined by 'x' ('60 x 40 x 30'). OCR sometimes splits that cell on the separator and shifts every column to its right by two, which slides the dimension figures into the weight columns and the real weights off the end of the row — a shipment whose gross weight becomes 30 kg instead of 368 kg. The specific numbers are chosen to be individually plausible in the wrong places: 40 equals row 1's real carton count, 30 and 25 read as small carton weights, and 62 x 62 makes the mis-split symmetric so the shift is not obvious from the values. The totals row deliberately leaves the dimension column blank (dimensions are not additive) while filling qty 2,100, ctns 95, net 987.50 and gross 1,118.00, all exact column sums — so a column shift that pushes dimension numbers into the weight columns fails the gate immediately.

title: Handwritten packing list with no ruled columns — refusal case
note: Sri Lanka · small textile consignment, hand-written note scanned as the packing list
page:

M/s SEA STAR TRADING (PVT) LTD
COLOMBO 15
Date 12/03/26

1. Cotton bed sheets - 20 ctns 340 kg
2. Pillow covers 8 ctns abt 96 kgs
3. Curtain cloth rolls — 5 rolls, 210 kg (gross)

| Total 33 ctns/rolls | 646 kgs gross approx. |
| --- | --- |

for SEA STAR TRADING
what_is_different: The scan has no ruled columns, so Mistral emits the goods as prose lines and only manages a degenerate two-cell table where the writer drew a rough line under the list. There is no header row, so there is no column map and nothing to anchor description, quantity, carton or weight against — the parser must decline the page rather than guess positions from the text order. Everything about the content also argues for refusal even if a grid could be forced: the weights are hedged ('abt 96 kgs', '646 kgs gross approx.'), net and gross are never distinguished (only line 3 says gross, and only for itself), and the units are mixed cartons and rolls so '33 ctns/rolls' is not a carton count. The figures happen to reconcile (20+8+5 = 33; 340+96+210 = 646), which is precisely the trap: an arithmetic-only gate would close on a page whose weight basis is unknown, and weight basis is what drives duty. Correct behaviour is refusal and escalation, not a plausible three-item table.

title: Packing list with no description column at all — item codes and weights only
note: Japan · automotive spare parts, code-only shipper packing list
what_is_different: There is no goods-description column anywhere on the page — the shipper identifies goods purely by part number, and a customs description has to fall back to the code (or be sourced from the invoice). A parser that requires a description header before it will own the table stands down here and hands a perfectly regular grid to the LLM. Second trap: there is no carton-COUNT column either, only carton-number RANGES; the counts (12, 8, 18) exist only as the width of '1-12', '13-20', '21-38', and the totals row prints the count '38 CTNS' inside the carton-NUMBER column, so the totals gate must compare 38 against summed range widths, not against a column it can read directly. The 'Rev' column (C, A, D) is a revision letter and must not be mistaken for a country of origin.

title: One product split across several rows, one row per carton size, with per-carton weights
note: Bangladesh · hosiery export, single style packed in three carton configurations
what_is_different: Every row is the SAME product and the same style number; the rows differ only by carton configuration (24, 12 and 6 dozen per carton). Nothing in the description distinguishes them, so a de-duplicator that collapses identical descriptions destroys two thirds of the shipment, while a merger that keeps three separate customs items over-fragments one HS line. PER-CARTON and PER-ROW weights sit in adjacent columns with near-identical headers: N.W./CTN 14.40 next to Total N.W. 720.00. Reading the per-carton column as the row weight declares 14.40 kg instead of 720.00 kg — a 50x understatement that no other number on a packing list contradicts, because only the totals row (1,008.00 / 1,099.00) is a sum of the TOTAL columns and the per-carton columns are deliberately left blank on the totals row. Both multiplications are printed and must hold: cartons x per-carton = total, for qty (50 x 24 = 1,200), net (50 x 14.40 = 720.00) and gross (50 x 15.50 = 775.00).

title: Packing list with pallet rows above their member carton rows (two-level hierarchy)
note: Malaysia · medical disposables, palletised export packing list with tare column
what_is_different: Three kinds of row share one grid: goods rows, packing-material rows (the two EUR PALLET lines, 0.00 net / 25.00 tare / 25.00 gross), and per-pallet SUB-TOTAL rows. Only three rows are goods. Counting all eight body rows gives eight items; counting the sub-totals gives double the weight. The GRAND TOTAL is an exact column sum of every non-subtotal row (192.00+288.00+0.00+300.00+0.00 = 780.00 net; 214.00+321.00+25.00+330.00+25.00 = 915.00 gross; 22.00+33.00+25.00+30.00+25.00 = 135.00 tare; 8+12+15 = 35 ctns), and each sub-total is an exact sum of its own block — so the printed-totals gate can only close if the pallet lines are treated as weight-bearing non-goods. Net + Tare = Gross holds on every row and on both sub-totals, which is the tare column's only cross-check; goods-row gross alone sums to 865.00, and the 50.00 kg shortfall against the printed 915.00 is the pallet timber, not a missing item.

Note also that the description cell carries digits ('5000mAh', '45W', '1.5M') that must not be harvested as numerics. title: USA · packing list in LBS with a parallel KGS conversion column
note: USA (Chicago) → industrial parts; imperial primary, metric conversion printed alongside
what_is_different: Every weight is printed twice, once in LBS and once converted to KGS, so there are FOUR weight columns and only two of them are declarable. The unit lives only in the header parenthesis, not in the cells. US locale: dot decimal with comma thousands, so '1,050.00' must not be read as 1.05 or as two cells. Row-wise rounding means the KGS totals are the sum of the rounded rows (884.50) rather than the conversion of the LBS total (884.51) — the totals gate must compare against the printed column sum, not re-derive it.

note: China → export electronics/accessories; classic Shenzhen forwarder layout

The printed total (387.00) matches only the TOTAL NET WT column, so the totals gate is the only thing that can tell them apart. Same shape for QTY/CTN (50) vs TOTAL QTY (1000).
